title: Pediatric Inventory for Parents (PIP) Protocol in Spanish Population
author: Marian Perez-Marin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.pvvdn66

steps.title: Recruit participants and collect questionnaires
steps.instruction: Recruit caregivers of pediatric patients following their medical appointment and doctor's presentation.

substeps.instruction: Obtain signed informed consent for voluntary and anonymous participation.
Provide a set of questionnaires to the caregiver.
Allow the caregiver to complete the questionnaires in the waiting area over 30 minutes.
Collect the completed questionnaires.

steps.title: Digitize data
steps.instruction: Create a database using SPSS 23.0 to digitize the obtained data.

steps.title: Divide sample for analysis
steps.instruction: Divide the total sample into two groups using cluster sampling based on age, sex, and diagnosis.

substeps.instruction: Assign Subsample A for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA).
Assign Subsample B for Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA).

steps.title: Perform initial item and reliability analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze item properties and instrument reliability using SPSS 23.0, EQS 6.3, and FACTOR software.

substeps.instruction: Observe item-total correlation coefficients.
Analyze variations in Cronbach's alpha coefficients if items are eliminated.
Calculate Cronbach’s alpha for psychometric properties.

steps.title: Conduct Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA)
steps.instruction: Perform EFA on Subsample A following the process recommended by Lloret-Segura et al.

substeps.instruction: Use the unweighted least-squares method (ULS).
Apply the method of parallel analysis.
Apply direct Oblimin rotation.

steps.title: Conduct Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA)
steps.instruction: Validate the factorial structure of the scales using Subsample B.

substeps.instruction: Use maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and the robust Satorra-Bentler adjustment to correct for absence of multivariate normality.
Test CFA adequacy using the significance of chi-squared and the robust Satorra-Bentler correction (S-B χ²).
Calculate χ² ratio and its degrees of freedom (χ²/df) and S-B X² and its degrees of freedom (values < 5 are acceptable).
Test goodness of fit using non-normed fit index (NNFI), comparative fit index (CFI), and incremental fit fix (IFI), where values > .90 indicate a good fit.
Compute root mean-square error of approximation (RMSEA), where values < .08 indicate a good fit.

steps.title: Analyze dimensions and validity
steps.instruction: Analyze relationships between instrument dimensions and establish criterion validity.

substeps.instruction: Perform Pearson correlation analysis among different dimensions of the instrument.
Perform Pearson’s correlations between PIP dimensions and HADS (anxiety and depression).
Perform hierarchical regressions to study the ability of PIP to predict anxiety and depression.

steps.title: Perform final statistical comparisons
steps.instruction: Analyze mean differences and calculate sample distributions.

substeps.instruction: Analyze mean differences in relation to diagnosis using ANOVA with Tukey post hoc.
Calculate centiles for the whole sample and for each pathology separately.
